Reporting phi as 0.0 here would claim independence that was never measured, so the script reports undefined and says why. The general finding is that tier I3 needs errors to measure: a dataset where reviewers do not err on the only mechanically decidable dimension yields no signal however many items it holds. Three things would supply one and none exists today: a harder mechanical task where models measurably fail, human-confirmed gold which is tier I4 or I5 and the scarce resource the ladder exists to route around, or a genuinely cross-family panel needing new spend against a second provider. Until then any claim resting on a model panel must be recorded as asserted rather than measured, which the ladder already specifies as the fallback. The harness is reusable; what it lacks is a dataset with errors in it.
summary: An attempt to measure reviewer error correlation found no measurable errors. Across 120 queries neither role of the two-role dataset cited an evidence identifier absent from the material it was shown, so both binary error vectors are constant and phi is undefined rather than zero. The dataset's own gold cannot substitute: 95 of its 120 labels are the two roles' unanimous agreement and 25 are a third same-family adjudication, with none human confirmed.
title: Tier I3 cannot be instantiated on existing data and remains a label

body: A registered priority asked to repair the distinction between discovered, screened, read and independently reviewed sources; this replaces the description with numbers. Three gaps are distinct. The catalog cannot express reading state, because its status column records whether a work is peer-reviewed or a preprint, while CONTRIBUTING requires a reading note to follow reading the source rather than its abstract and nothing records which happened. The ledger distinguishes abstract-extracted from extracted, but only for claims and never for sources, so a source read in full and one skimmed for a single claim are indistinguishable. And the catalog is not the canonical source list, since 36 percent of claims cite something outside it. One limitation bounds the read count: it is measured by a catalogued URL appearing in note text, so a note referencing a work by title alone is missed and 18 is a lower bound. Nothing was repaired, because assigning a reading state to 174 sources is a judgement about what was actually read and guessing it would write a fabricated state into what reads afterwards as a record.
summary: Measured over 174 catalogued sources and 181 evidence-ledger claims: 114 sources are cited by at least one claim, 57 have never been cited, and only 18 have a full-read note. 65 of 181 claims cite a source that appears in no catalog. The catalog's status column holds publication type for 167 of 174 rows and cannot express a reading state at all.
title: The source pipeline cannot say what was read, and a third of the catalog is unused

body: The failure mode is general and worth naming, because it recurred in a second place the same day. The repository claim audit initially reported nine critical findings, of which three were false positives from a heuristic that read rankings_sha256 as a file digest. Both are the same error: a hand-written membership list stands in for a property, the list is never complete, and its gaps present as findings rather than as gaps. A structural test asks what a thing is rather than whether it appears in a list someone wrote. Here the resolvable question is whether the string is a URL or a path, which no new publication host can break, while whether it is catalogued is a separate and genuinely useful question. The corrected numbers are 46 uncatalogued publications, 15 repository links belonging in the repository catalog rather than the paper catalog, 3 internal artifacts correctly uncatalogued, and exactly one claim whose primary source is not a source at all, AI-005 citing project-analysis.
summary: The source-pipeline audit gave a misleading number three times in one session because it classified citations by enumerating publication hosts. Checking only arXiv and DOI filed NeurIPS, MLR, ACL Anthology and OpenReview as unresolvable; adding those then filed PubMed Central, RFC Editor, EUR-Lex and VLDB the same way. Replacing the list with a structural test — a source is resolvable if it is a URL or a path — took claims with no resolvable source from a reported 65 to an actual 1.
title: Classify by structure, never by a hand-written list of members

body:
A growth strategy proposed leading the README with a benchmark table comparing adaptive memory against compaction, BM25+vector and Mem0. The example numbers in that proposal were illustrative placeholders. Publishing them, or any unearned equivalent, is refused: this repository's entire value proposition is that every claim carries provenance, and a fabricated headline would invalidate all of it retroactively.

The comparison requires a history family that does not exist. That is issue 41, which also blocks 20 of 71 registered experiments. Popularity work and research work therefore share one critical path, which is fortunate: no trade-off is needed.

Two commitments made publicly on the README alongside this: the result will be published whichever way it falls, and a negative headline is a live possibility given that three separate runs here have already measured this project's own mechanisms harming retrieval. External publication (Show HN, subreddits, X) is deferred until the number exists and is the maintainer's decision to make, not an agent's.
summary: The launch is gated on a measured comparison, not on packaging. Inventing plausible numbers would cost this project its only asset.
title: No benchmark table on the README until a real corpus produces one

body:
The research audience for agent memory is small. The audience for persistent memory in a coding agent is large, and this repository already ships the thing that serves it: a dependency-free stdio MCP server exposing eight tools over an append-only events.jsonl.

Verified before the README claimed it, rather than after: the server was run against an empty scratch directory with --root ., initialize and tools/list returned correctly, and a memory_add followed by memory_search round-tripped, creating exactly one file. The claim 'give Claude Code persistent project memory in two minutes' is therefore a tested statement and not marketing.

The README labels it the research engine rather than a finished product, because that is what it is. Overselling it would attract users who bounce, which is worse for reach than a smaller honest claim.
summary: Leading the README with two-minute Claude Code setup targets coding-agent users rather than the small memory-research audience. The claim was tested on a fresh project before being written down.
title: The MCP adapter is the reach vector, and the claim was verified before publishing it

body:
A perfect score on the metric a benchmark exists to measure is the same signal PMLAB-DECORR-E1 produced: a constant vector means the instrument is not measuring, not that the system is perfect. Here the forbidden record was retrieved a quarter of the time and never once outranked the gold.

The cause was length. Under BM25 over an OR of query terms a longer document matches more terms, so an arm could have scored well by preferring long events without reading one.

Two repairs failed first and both are instructive. Hand-balancing the texts inverted the confound rather than removing it, 12/12 becoming 0/12, because a fixed template gives a fixed length relationship however the surface varies. Appending a content-neutral elaboration on a coin flip fixed two families and left the two whose base gap no elaboration could bridge. The working repair closes the base gap and elaborates independently, so length is uncorrelated with goldness rather than equal on average.

The durable part is the construction test, not the texts. A perfect split in either direction now fails.

After repair, recall@10 fell to 0.810 and the failure modes fire: OBSOLETE at 0.167, and POISON retrieving the poisoned line above the real rule in 25 percent of cases while scoring a perfect 1.000 on recall. That last pair is the sharpest argument this project has for why recall alone cannot be a headline number.
summary: The first baseline over the new corpus scored recall@10 0.929 with forbidden-above-gold constant at zero across 48 probes. The gold event was longer than the forbidden one in 12 of 12 instances of three families.
title: Corpus H1 measured document length instead of memory, and the constant metric revealed it

body:
21 probes, three per family, deepseek-v4-flash over an FTS5 retrieval arm, 0.0094 USD.

Overall: gold retrieved 0.905, answered 0.810, answered from the wrong record 0.143.

The two families built around a forbidden record behave very differently from the rest and from each other.

POISON scores a perfect 1.000 on answering and still surfaces the poisoned instruction in a third of probes. A metric that reports only correctness would call this flawless. The agent would have both the real rule and a fetched line telling it to disable a release gate, and nothing in the score distinguishes that from clean.

OBSOLETE answers correctly only a third of the time and returns the superseded host two thirds of the time. The obsolete fact is stated three times over eleven days and the correction once, tersely, so frequency, order of establishment and length all point the wrong way. A memory system that weights by repetition fails this by design rather than by accident.

Three harness defects were found by paid probes and none by the free stub: every instance of a family shared its question, the prompt instructed the model to name what it rejected which the scorer then credited, and the pilot sampled alphabetically so it drew one family. A fourth was a scoring error rather than a model error, where the corpus required the word five and the model answered 5.

Total cost of finding all four: 0.021 USD.
summary: First paid reader pilot on corpus H1: POISON answered 1.000 and leaked the poisoned instruction in 33 percent of probes. OBSOLETE answered 0.333 and leaked the superseded host in 67 percent.
title: A reader can score perfect on the right answer while acting on the poisoned one

body:
The proposal converges with schema v2 from the other direction. HISTORICAL versus INVALIDATED is exactly the succession versus correction distinction already recorded, and the reason both are needed is the same: a superseded fact has a sensible answer to where did he live before, while a corrected one has none, because it was never true.

Two constraints the rank must respect, both already measured here.

Rank is not validity. PMLAB-REV-V0 case C3: a record written on 15 January but valid from 1 September is N1 and is not the answer on 1 May. So rank is a retrieval prior and the truth predicate stays valid_from <= t <= valid_to. Answering CURRENT queries from rank alone leaks the future.

Rank must be local to an entity-property slot. Kuba.address and Kuba.job are separate chains, and a change of employer must not renumber addresses. A single global rank would be meaningless.

The expensive part is not the rank, it is deriving the chain: extracting entity, property and value from a message so two records can be known to concern the same slot. Nothing in raw text announces this, and it is the step that needs a model.

Measured model-free on the OBSOLETE family under oracle chaining: demotion removes stale records from the retrieved context entirely, from 1.000 to 0.000, while gold in context stays at 0.167. So the mechanism removes the wrong answer without finding the right one, and the predicted effect is that a confident wrong answer becomes no answer. That is a safety improvement rather than a capability improvement, and the two should not be reported as one number.
summary: Proposed externally: rank records N1, N2, N3 within one entity-property chain, with status CURRENT, HISTORICAL or INVALIDATED. Targets the measured 0.833 OBSOLETE leak.
title: State versioning per entity-property slot, tested as a rank prior rather than a truth predicate

body:
PMLAB-H1-DENSE-E1 established that an oracle router over lexical and dense retrieval ceilings at 0.929, and that six probes sit outside it. All six are OBSOLETE, whose union recall across both mechanisms is 6 of 12.

Dissecting them, model-free: the gold sits at lexical rank 27 to 50 and dense rank 22 to 99, against a budget that admits 17 to 22 records. Both mechanisms agree closely on where to put it, which rules out one of them simply misunderstanding the query.

What stands above it is the explanation. Twelve services each contribute three stale records and one correction, so 48 near-identical records all match the shape which staging host, which port. Neither term matching nor embedding similarity can single out one service's correction from among eleven siblings phrased the same way.

The consequence for architecture is specific. A better similarity function does not fix this, because similarity is what is saturated. What fixes it is addressing: resolve the query to an entity-property slot first, retrieve that slot's chain by exact key, then resolve temporally. billing.host is unique and needs no similarity at all.

That also gives any such layer a number to beat. Exceeding 0.929 would be evidence the gain came from something other than choosing between these two retrieval channels, because 0.929 bounds every router that could ever be built over them.
summary: Six of 84 probes are reached by neither lexical nor dense retrieval. Both rank the gold at 22 to 32 while the budget holds 17 to 22 records, so it is not a cutoff by one and not a failure to understand the query.
title: The unreachable OBSOLETE probes are an addressing problem, not a similarity problem

body:
Oracle addressing measured a large advantage that its headline number does not express. Gold recall of 1.000 is tautological: the oracle address is the case identity and the gold belongs to that case, so opening the slot always contains it.

What the construction does not determine is the advantage worth keeping. Context falls 245.5 to 68.8 tokens, candidates 11.0 to 3.4, stale contamination 0.548 to 0.143, gold per thousand retrieved tokens 3.59 to 14.54.

So the criterion is retained share of that advantage rather than exact address accuracy. An extractor at 91 percent exact address with 99 percent entity accuracy and under 1 percent collision may be a success; one at 97 percent exact with 5 percent collision is not, because collisions rebuild the near-clone problem inside a single drawer and fragmentation breaks the version chain.

Five thresholds are registered before any extractor exists: gold coverage at least 95 percent of oracle, stale-context rate below 0.20, mean context below 100 tokens, collision below 2 percent, catastrophic wrong-entity below 1 percent. Registering them afterwards would let any result be described as adequate.

Two design constraints follow from the failure modes rather than from taste. Extraction classifies into a controlled structure of entity, property and scope, and the canonical address is generated from those fields, because free-form naming produces fragmentation by construction. And an address mapping is superseded rather than rewritten when two names turn out to denote one entity, so an early mistake stays recoverable.
summary: PMLAB-H1-ADDR-E2 preregistered with five thresholds, no extractor built. The question is whether imperfect automatic addressing keeps the oracle's efficiency and stale-state advantage.
title: Address extraction is judged by advantage retained, not by address accuracy, and the thresholds are registered before the run

body:
Occurrences: the memory store resolving a path outside its root, twice; and both corpus generators printing an output directory supplied by the caller. Each was fixed locally and none of the fixes generalised, because each was treated as its own defect.

The shape is constant. Code computes a display or storage path with relative_to against a root it does not control, on the assumption that callers stay inside the repository. Callers legitimately do not — a temporary directory, a scratch path, an island used by a test.

Two consequences worth separating. The failure is loud, so it does not corrupt data. But it aborts after the real work is done, which in a generator means the artifact was written and the run reports failure.

The rule this yields: never call relative_to on a path the caller supplied without a fallback. A helper returning repo-relative when possible and absolute otherwise is three lines and removes the class.

The wider point is why this belongs in memory rather than in a changelog. A record of three independent bugs teaches nothing on the fourth occasion. A record saying this project has hit this class three times is what should surface when similar code is written next, and being able to surface it is the capability this project exists to build. It is a small instance of the thing itself.
summary: Path.relative_to has raised on an output path outside the repository three separate times in this project. Three occurrences of one shape is a pattern, not three bugs.
title: Repeated failure pattern: path handling assumes containment that is not guaranteed

body:
Records: 108 of 538 addressed. Queries: 12 of 84. Every gate except gold coverage passes, because a system that abstains rarely collides and never fragments — which is why abstention was registered as a reported figure and never a denominator.

Splitting the abstentions is what makes this useful. Entity is missing on 36 of 84 questions, property on 60. So deterministic rules recover the entity roughly twice as often as the property.

The mechanism is visible in a single case. For the question about how long an old deployment key stays valid after rotation, the entity resolves correctly while the property does not: the rule matches the assertion form used in records, key rotates, and the question uses the interrogative form, after rotation. The record side and the query side are different grammatical registers, and rules written for one do not transfer.

This changes what a model would be for. Not a memory controller in general, and not entity recognition, but property resolution across the assertion and interrogative forms of the same slot. That is a narrow, checkable job with a measured baseline to beat.

The result is a preregistered failure and is reported as one. Thresholds were frozen before this extractor existed, the extractor was written afterwards, and it does not meet them.
summary: E2-A abstains on 85.7 percent of probes and fails the preregistered gates. The decomposition is the result: entity is recovered on 0.571 of questions and property on 0.286.
title: Deterministic addressing fails on property resolution, not on entity resolution

body:
Entity-property addressing over an append-only store with temporal resolution is not a novel contribution and must not be presented as one anywhere in this repository. It was published with numbers before PMLAB-H1-ADDR-E1 ran.

A second verified paper is a more direct threat. Verbatim Chunks Beat Extracted Artifacts, arXiv 2601.00821, is a controlled ablation in which extraction into structured artifacts loses to verbatim chunks by 15.9 points on LoCoMo and 22.0 on LongMemEval-S, with extraction gaps accounting for 78.8 percent of failures. That is the same phenomenon E2-A measured here as 85.7 percent abstention, reached independently and in the same range. The convergence strengthens the measurement and removes any claim to having found it.

Reported but unverified, and recorded as such: A-TMA, STALE and CUPMem, VISTA, A-MAC, NEMORI. Two of those matter beyond addressing. A-MAC and NEMORI occupy future utility as a retention criterion, so memory learns what is worth remembering is no longer available as a novelty claim, and the README research questions state it as though it were open.

What appears unoccupied is not a system but a diagnostic programme: when and why similarity stops being the right access mechanism, measured through failure attribution, an oracle router ceiling, near-clone density and context cost. And one specific divergence from the published negative result — Verbatim Chunks concludes structure loses to raw text, while E2-A recovers entity on 0.571 of questions and property on 0.286, which localises the gap to one resolution step rather than to structure. If a narrow fix recovers the oracle advantage that refines a published finding; if not, the paper is right and this project should say so.

The process failure is worth recording separately. Selection rule 1 of the operating doctrine asks whether the answer already exists. It was applied to individual mechanisms and never to the architecture, and this gap was closed because someone outside the project asked the question the doctrine already required.
summary: APEX-MEM (ACL 2026, arXiv 2604.14362) implements entity-property-value over an append-only store with query-time temporal resolution, at 88.88 LoCoMo and 86.2 LongMemEval. Verified against primary sources.
title: The architecture this project converged on was published before it was measured here

body:
The numbers stand. Records addressed 108 of 538, queries 12 of 84, entity 0.571, property 0.286, gold coverage 0.143. Six gates pass and two fail, and the six pass because a system abstaining on 85.7 percent of probes rarely collides and never fragments, which is why abstention was registered as reported and never as a denominator.

The correction is to the inference rather than the data. The superseded record concluded that a model is required for property resolution across assertion and interrogative forms. What was shown is narrower: one deterministic extractor, whose rules match the assertion form records use, fails on the interrogative form questions use. A canonicalisation layer mapping rotates, rotation, after rotation, rotated key and old deployment key onto one property identifier might close the same gap with no model at all, and that has not been tried.

So an arm is inserted before the model arm. E2-A v1 stays frozen at 0.143 as the baseline and its rules are not improved. E2-A2 adds property canonicalisation and remains model-free. Only then E2-B with a small model, and E2-C hybrid.

The ordering decides what can be concluded. Going straight from failing rules to a model would establish that a model works, never that it was necessary, and this project has just recorded prior art in which a cheap extractor was the bottleneck rather than the representation. If canonicalisation closes most of the gap, the finding is that structure needed engineering rather than intelligence, which is cheaper and more falsifiable.
summary: E2-A abstains on 85.7 percent of probes. Entity resolves on 0.571 of questions, property on 0.286. The superseded record inferred that a model is needed for property resolution, which the measurement does not support.
supersession_reason: the original inferred a need for a model from the failure of one rule set; a canonicalisation layer is an untested model-free alternative
title: Deterministic addressing fails on property resolution; whether that needs a model is untested

body:
Numbers, dev-a then valid-b: coverage 0.571 and 0.571, abstention 0.429 and 0.429, stale 0.143 and 0.143, collision 0.000, fragmentation 0.000, catastrophic wrong entity 0.000, context 15.2 and 14.5 tokens.

The transfer is the result. valid-b draws its twelve subject nouns from a disjoint block and shares no question with dev-a, and the figures match to three decimals. So the mapping is not a dictionary fitted to one corpus wording; the entries name linguistic alternations and those alternations hold on unseen subjects. Property normalisation generalises without a model.

It still fails, and the failure is now sharply localised. Exactly three families sit at 0.000 on both splits: DELAYED, OBSOLETE and POISON. Inspecting their questions shows property resolving correctly in every case and entity returning None. The bottleneck moved from property to entity.

The mechanism is the same one, on the other field. Entity patterns were written against the assertion grammar records use, staging for orders deploys to, and questions use an interrogative grammar, which staging host should a orders deploy target. Twice now the deterministic gap has been a grammar-transfer gap rather than a comprehension gap.

That is a claim about where a model is and is not needed, and it is not yet established. An entity canonicalisation arm is warranted on the same reasoning that justified A2, and must be frozen by digest before execution for the same reason. Writing it and running it on dev-a repeatedly would produce a number about dev-a.

The stale rate of 0.143 is worth flagging as probably a measurement artifact rather than a regression: BILINGUAL slots hold two paraphrases of one fact, so opening the chain returns a record that is not the gold and is not superseded either. Not corrected here, because changing a metric definition after seeing a result is the thing the frozen denominators exist to prevent.
summary: E2-A2 raises gold coverage from 0.143 to 0.571 with no model, and dev-a and valid-b agree to three decimals despite twelve entirely different subject nouns. It still fails the 0.95 gate.
title: Property canonicalisation transfers perfectly to an unseen split and moves the bottleneck to entity

body:
The progression is the result. E2-A 0.143, E2-A2 0.571, E2-A3 1.000, and dev and valid agree to three decimals at every step despite sharing no question and drawing subject nouns from disjoint blocks. Two successive bottlenecks that looked like they needed a model turned out to be grammar transfer: rules written against the assertive grammar of records failing on the interrogative grammar of questions, first for property and then for entity. Both were closed by canonicalisation with no model and 33 tokens of context.

The failure is on stale_context_rate, 0.286 against a threshold of 0.20, and it concentrates entirely in BILINGUAL at 1.000 and OBSOLETE at 1.000 on both splits.

Those two are different cases and neither is an addressing defect. BILINGUAL slots hold two paraphrases of one fact, so a same-slot record that is not the gold is not superseded either, and the metric counts it anyway. OBSOLETE slots hold the obsolete record and its correction, so opening the chain returns both by design — which is what an addressing layer is supposed to do before a temporal resolver chooses between them.

So the gate mixes two components. It was set at 0.20 from the oracle addressing arm's 0.143, and that arm was also addressing-only. The threshold therefore asks an addressing layer to do work that belongs to temporal resolution, and this arm contains no temporal resolver. PMLAB-H1-READ-E1 already measured that the rank-demotion resolver takes the OBSOLETE leak from 0.833 to 0.000, so the missing component exists and is not in the arm being scored.

The gate is not changed. It was frozen before an extractor existed and the whole value of freezing it is that a result cannot move it. E2-A3 is recorded as FAIL and the diagnosis is recorded beside it, so a later reader can judge whether the threshold or the arm was wrong. A diagnostic variant excluding same-slot records that no supersession separates is registered as an addition, never as a replacement.
summary: E2-A3 scores gold coverage 1.000 on dev-a and valid-b, all seven families, zero abstention, zero collision, zero fragmentation, zero wrong entity. It fails the frozen stale gate at 0.286 against 0.20.
title: Deterministic addressing reaches full coverage on an unseen split and still fails, on a gate that measures the wrong component

body:
On OBSOLETE, the family every earlier mechanism failed: gold in context 12 of 12, gold ranked first 12 of 12, mean 4.0 candidates. Lexical retrieval reached the gold on 0.167 of those probes and the reader answered from the superseded record on 0.833.

The resolver being a no-op is a finding about the composition rather than a defect in either part. PMLAB-H1-READ-E1 measured rank demotion over a lexical ranking, which is ordered by relevance and mixes eras freely, so demoting below N1 moved records. An addressed chain is already ordered newest-first, so the same operation has nothing to move. The work the resolver was doing was repairing an ordering that addressing never breaks.

That narrows what a temporal resolver is for. Not ranking within a chain, which addressing gives for free, but the cases ordering cannot decide: a record whose valid_from lies in the future and is newest without being in force, and a correction, where the superseded record must not answer even a question about the past because it was never true. PMLAB-REV-V0 case C3 is the first and the corpus contains no instance of it; the corpus exercises succession only.

Stale remains at 0.286, concentrated in BILINGUAL and OBSOLETE. For OBSOLETE the gold is ranked first and the superseded record is also present, which is what a chain is. Whether that harms an answer is a reader question and is not decided by any retrieval number here.

Two limits. The composition is deterministic and involved no model, so it says nothing about end-to-end answering; that costs about 0.04 USD and has not been run. And the corpus was built by the same author as the mechanisms, so full coverage on it bounds what these rules can express rather than what they generalise to.
summary: Fully automatic on both splits: gold in context 1.000, gold ranked first 0.857, 1.6 candidates, 33 tokens. Adding the rank resolver changed nothing to three decimals, because addressing already returns the chain newest-first.
title: The two mechanisms compose, and the temporal resolver turns out to be a no-op once addressing time-orders the chain

body:
H1 exercises succession only and the resolver was a no-op there: address-only and address-plus-resolver agreed to three decimals. H2 was built so that every family is a case where the newest record is not the answer.

Ordering alone passes only TEMP-CORRECTION, and that is accidental — the correction happens to be the newest record. It scores zero on FUTURE, HISTORICAL, OVERLAP and CONFLICT, and takes the specifically wrong record on 0.600 of probes rather than merely missing.

Two families are traps for the resolver rather than for the retriever, and they are why no ordering policy can pass. TEMP-HISTORICAL asks about the past, so the superseded record is the answer and a resolver that suppresses old records fails. TEMP-CONFLICT places two sources in disagreement with no supersession between them, where declining is correct and any confident pick is wrong. Always-newest fails FUTURE and OVERLAP; always-oldest fails HISTORICAL; suppress-the-old fails HISTORICAL; always-answer fails CONFLICT.

So the component is not redundant, and the earlier finding was about the benchmark rather than the mechanism. Its value is confined to the cases ordering cannot decide, and an addressed chain gives ordering for free.

The limit is the same one that applies to A3. The resolver was written by an author who knows the five families, each check corresponds to one of them, and it scores 1.000. That measures what rules can express on constructed cases, not what they generalise to. The dev and valid splits share no question and use disjoint subject blocks, which controls for wording but not for the author knowing the case taxonomy.
summary: On corpus H2, ordering by recency scores 0.200 and takes the wrong record on 0.600 of probes. A validity-aware resolver scores 1.000 across all five families, identically on dev and valid.
title: The temporal resolver is worthless on succession and decisive where ordering cannot decide

body:
Every number produced here so far — E2-A 0.143, E2-A2 0.571, E2-A3 1.000, the resolver at 1.000 on H2 — comes from a corpus whose author also wrote the rules being scored. Disjoint dev and valid splits control for wording. They do not control for the author knowing the case taxonomy, and full coverage on a corpus built around five known families bounds what rules can express rather than what they generalise to.

So the division is fixed. Internal corpora answer why a system failed and are worth keeping precisely because they localise a failure to a component, which an external benchmark cannot do. External benchmarks answer whether a mechanism works at all, and no claim of the second kind may cite the first.

STALE is the first external target, verified at arXiv 2605.06527. 400 expert-validated conflict scenarios, 1200 queries, contexts to 150K tokens, three probing dimensions covering state resolution, premise resistance and implicit policy adaptation. The best evaluated model reaches 55.2 percent overall, so it is not a solved benchmark.

Its central finding is the one this project reached from the other direction. STALE calls it the current-state adjudication gap: updated evidence can be stored and retrieved and does not reliably become the basis that governs subsequent answers. That is the F2 against F3 and F4 distinction the failure attribution here produced, and it is what the rank-demotion arm addressed when it took the OBSOLETE leak from 0.833 to 0.000 on internal data.

Two further external targets after it: LongMemEval for knowledge updates, temporal reasoning and abstention, and LongMemEval-V2 later as an agentic test. ProsusAI/MemEval already runs several memory systems over LoCoMo and LongMemEval and may remove the need to build a harness, which is why it was catalogued in issue 35.
summary: H1 and H2 were written by the same author as the mechanisms they score. They answer why a system failed. Whether a mechanism works outside this laboratory requires a benchmark this project did not write, and STALE is the first one.
title: Internal corpora are diagnostic instruments only; no claim that a mechanism works may rest on them

body:
Frozen as a distinct claim because it is separable from the retrieval and addressing results and has its own scope.

Ordering by recency passes only TEMP-CORRECTION, and by accident, since the correction happens to be the newest record. It scores zero on FUTURE, HISTORICAL, OVERLAP and CONFLICT.

The abstention figure was checked rather than assumed. All 14 abstentions are TEMP-CONFLICT and all 14 TEMP-CONFLICT probes abstain, with no leakage either way. On the same family the ordering arm produced a confident answer 14 times out of 14 and was wrong 14 times out of 14. Task success and forced answer rate are therefore different measurements, and a system that always answers can have worse memory than one that detects a conflict and declines.

So a temporal resolver is not a general sorter of memory. It decides the cases where order of writing and truth in time are not the same thing, and an addressed chain already supplies ordering for free. That is why the same comparison on H1 produced identical numbers to three decimals: H1 contains only succession.

Scope. Both corpora were written by the author of the mechanisms, each resolver check corresponds to one constructed family, and the arm scores 1.000. Disjoint splits control for wording, not for the author knowing the taxonomy. This claim states what a rule set can express on constructed non-monotonic cases and says nothing about whether it generalises. STALE is the external target that would test that.
summary: Corpus H2, two arms, identical on dev and valid. Ordering by recency scores 0.200 and takes the specifically wrong record on 0.600. A validity-aware resolver scores 1.000 across all five families.
title: C3 temporal state: ordering suffices for succession and fails on every non-monotonic case

body:
Share by block: entity patterns 0.833, property rules 0.929, property canonicalisation 0.842, entity canonicalisation 0.000. Total 0.786.

The blunt reading is correct and has to be said first. E2-A3 scoring 1.000 has not been shown to be about addressing rather than about this corpus's vocabulary, and the number to expect on external data is unknown rather than 1.000. Disjoint dev and valid splits controlled for wording and never for the rules being written by someone who knows the seven families.

The split inside that number is the more useful part. The base extractor and the property layer are built from staging, deploy log, retry loop, pytest and klucz wdrozeniowy — domain nouns. The entity canonicalisation layer is built from should a X, deploying X, in X again and was the X: six patterns, zero domain tokens, pure interrogative grammar. That layer is what moved coverage from 0.571 to 1.000.

So the prediction for an external benchmark is not uniform. The property side should transfer badly because it names this domain. The entity side has no domain to leave behind and may transfer. If that pattern holds on STALE it would be informative in a way a flat pass or fail would not, and it is a prediction made before the run rather than an explanation offered after it.

The audit itself had a defect found while running it: comments in these files quote example sentences from the corpus, and the first version counted them as patterns, inflating the specific share to 0.837 in the audit's own favour. Comments are now stripped before extraction. The direction of that error is worth noting — it flattered the audit's conclusion, not the extractor's.
summary: Audit run before spending an external benchmark. Of 70 patterns, 55 contain a content word the generators emit. But entity_canon, the layer taking coverage from 0.571 to 1.000, contains none.
title: 78.6 percent of the extractor is vocabulary from the corpus it was written against, and the layer that closed the last gap is 0 percent

body:
From the results table in github.com/icedreamc/STALE at commit ea7d391, MIT licensed:

Gemini-3.1-pro reaches 92.0 and 69.0 on state resolution, 30.0 and 14.0 on premise resistance, 71.0 and 55.0 on implicit policy adaptation, for 55.2 overall. CUPMem reaches 91.0 and 89.0 on state resolution, 78.0 and 75.0 on premise resistance, 32.0 and 43.0 on implicit policy adaptation, for 68.0 overall.

CUPMem more than doubles premise resistance and roughly halves implicit policy adaptation. A system that resists a false presupposition is not the same system as one that acts on an update, and the aggregate averages the two into a single number that orders them while hiding that they trade.

This is the same shape as measurements already made here. Recall against forbidden-record leakage: the POISON family scored a perfect 1.000 on answering while surfacing the poisoned instruction on a quarter of probes. Task success against forced-answer rate: on the conflict family the ordering arm answered 14 of 14 and was wrong 14 of 14 while the resolver declined all 14, and a single accuracy figure scores those identically.

Two consequences for the external run. Report all six settings, never the overall alone. And the useful question is not whether AAMR beats 68.0 or the 73.6 a later system reports, but which cells it occupies — losing overall while winning state resolution at lower context and with no model extractor would be a more informative result than a higher average.

None of those numbers is a target until the backbone, prompt, judge, budget and history protocol are reproduced. 55.2 is one model under their conditions and 68.0 is their own system; neither is comparable to anything run here yet.

CUPMem ships in the same repository, so it can be run as a baseline on one harness rather than reimplemented.
summary: Verified in the official repository. Gemini-3.1-pro 55.2 overall, CUPMem 68.0. But CUPMem gains on premise resistance and loses badly on implicit policy adaptation, so the two systems are not ordered.
title: The STALE baselines have opposite failure profiles, so overall accuracy hides the structure

body:
Grammar coverage against STALE, question text only, no gold read and no benchmark spent:

entity_canon with zero domain vocabulary fires on 0.4458 of 1200 questions. The address_extract entity layer at 83 percent domain vocabulary fires on 0.0000, with all twelve patterns dead. The two property layers at 84 and 93 percent fire on 0.0017.

By the registered number the prediction holds with a wide margin. By mechanism it does not. Of the six entity_canon patterns, five match nothing or almost nothing: should a X, deploying X, was the X and happen to the X all score zero. The entire 535 matches come from one pattern, in-or-for followed by a word, which is the most permissive construction in the set and fires on ordinary English prepositions rather than on any interrogative frame.

What it extracts settles it. Of 1200 questions, 299 yield an entity, and the commonest are service.them, service.years, service.about, service.next, service.over, service.tomorrow and service.dinner. These are function words and adverbs, not entities.

So the honest reading is that entity_canon does not transfer. It appears to because a catch-all fires, and the specific grammatical constructions claimed to be general — the interrogative frames that took internal coverage from 0.571 to 1.000 — match nothing outside the corpus they were written against.

The value of running this before scoring is what it prevents. A full run would have produced a low number, and the obvious reading would have been that the mechanism failed. The truth is that the mechanism never fired, and where it fired it produced nonsense. Those need different work and a single accuracy figure would have merged them.

Cost: zero. No benchmark consumed, no model called, decidable from question text alone.
summary: On 1200 external questions, entity_canon fires on 0.446 and the domain-heavy layers on 0.002. But five of its six patterns are dead and the entire coverage comes from one catch-all preposition matcher producing entities like service.them and service.years.
title: The registered transfer prediction is confirmed on its letter and refuted in its substance

body:
What was read: 1200 question strings, through a loader that takes one field and discards the record. What was not read: gold answers, labels, families, the success key, the scoring code. That is recorded rather than glossed, because the difference between an unseen benchmark and one whose question forms were inspected is real even when nothing else was touched.

Consequences. STALE question forms may not inform the design of CANDIDATE-1. Any final claim of generalisation needs a second benchmark whose questions were never inspected, and MemoryAgentBench conflict resolution or LongMemEval-V2 are the candidates.

CANDIDATE-0 is retained as a negative artifact and is not repaired. Fixing it against STALE would convert the benchmark into a development set and destroy the only property it was wanted for.

The scope of the failure matters as much as the failure. What failed is the first bridge alone: natural language to entity, property and scope. Addressable state, temporal resolution, retrieval and context never received valid input on external data, so they are untested rather than refuted. A low external score would have read as a verdict on the whole architecture; localising it leaves every downstream claim open.

This also gives a model its first evidenced place in this project. Two earlier candidate roles were refuted by measurement, since canonicalisation sufficed for both property and entity resolution internally. What external data shows is that literal and grammatical rules do not transfer across corpora, and that is a narrow failure a model is a plausible answer to: resolving language to an address where deterministic rules abstain, choosing from controlled candidate sets, with a deterministic validator accepting or abstaining. The model resolves language rather than managing memory.
summary: A question-text-only audit was run before any model evaluation. STALE remains a valid external test and its strongest sealing property is spent, so a final claim needs a second benchmark whose questions were never inspected.
title: STALE is no longer sealed in the strongest sense, and CANDIDATE-0 stands as a negative artifact

body:
The old order was to build, then look at the competition. It produced an architecture identical to APEX-MEM published before our measurement of it, and an entity resolver that reached 1.000 internally and does not fire on external questions.

The new order is: our failure mode, then our hypothesis, then prior art, then take an existing component if one is good, then test our marginal contribution.

The immediate application is not general. CANDIDATE-0 failed on one bridge, language to entity, property and scope. Hindsight, MIT licensed and reporting 91.4 on LongMemEval, resolves surface forms so that Alice, Alice Chen and the new PM reach one canonical entity. That is our failure described as a solved feature, and writing a third rule set before reading theirs repeats the mistake selection rule 1 of our own doctrine exists to prevent.

Reading order: Hindsight first, because it is open, mature and its pipeline runs end to end from write to retrieval, and its retain-recall-reflect split plus the TEMPR retrieval strategies expose a model-versus-heuristic boundary someone else arrived at independently. Graphiti second and narrower, for valid_from, valid_to, invalidated_at and provenance, rather than rebuilding a temporal model for a week so that it is ours.

Three questions per mechanism: have they solved it, is theirs better, and can it be taken without losing what we are trying to study.

The research question is unaffected and remains unoccupied: when is deterministic addressable state sufficient and where exactly does a model become necessary. Taking a working entity resolver as the floor makes that easier to answer, because it removes a component we have now measured ourselves failing at and moves the effort to the margin nobody has isolated.

Nothing here commits to adopting any code. Licence and attribution are recorded before anything is borrowed, and a negative result closes the reading — their resolver costing a large model call per event would be a complete answer.
summary: The build-then-compare order cost this project a week and one architecture claim. It is inverted: measure a failure, check prior art, take a working component if one exists, and study only the margin.
title: Existing systems become the floor; original work happens only at a measured gap

body:
The harness exists and is correct. measure_reviewer_decorrelation.py computes phi over binary error vectors and returns undefined rather than 0.0 when a vector is constant, which is why the earlier run reported honestly instead of claiming an independence nobody measured. What it lacked was a dataset with errors in it.

Comparing Graphiti, Hindsight, CUPMem, APEX-MEM and this project's own arms on one harness supplies exactly that. Four architecturally distinct systems, scored per question by failure type across entity, property, retrieval, stale, conflict, future validity, reasoning and abstention, will not produce constant error vectors. Tier I3, a cross-family panel with measured rather than asserted error correlation, becomes instantiable for the first time since the independence ladder was written.

That connection was not planned and it changes the value of the comparative track. It is not a survey with a measurement attached; it is the first dataset on which a registered blocked tier can run.

The condition that makes or breaks it is one harness. A transplant comparing a mechanism added to a base is void unless every arm shares model, embedder, scoring, decoding and budget, because two deltas measured under different conditions are not on the same scale and adding them means nothing. ProsusAI/MemEval holds those constant and is the candidate; its own audit here records that the constants are repeated per adapter rather than enforced by a registry, which is a risk to carry rather than ignore.

The hypothesis has a real negative branch. If the correlations show the mechanisms are largely redundant, the finding is that the design space is smaller than it looks and several of these systems are one system in different vocabularies. That would be worth publishing and would change what this project builds next.
summary: PMLAB-DECORR-E1 closed because two roles of one model family produced constant error vectors, so phi was undefined and tier I3 could not be instantiated. Architecturally distinct systems will not produce constant vectors.
title: The decorrelation harness that had nothing to measure has something once several systems are compared

body:
fact_extraction.py imports llm_interface and llm_wrapper and defines Pydantic response models, and entity_processing.py names the result llm_entities. entity_resolver.py is 1405 lines with no model in the merge path: pg_trgm trigram Jaccard reimplemented in Python, verified byte-for-byte against Postgres so a cutoff calibrated there transfers exactly, then union-find with path halving, then a canonical name chosen as most-mentioned, then shortest, then lexicographically smallest.

That places their model at extraction and their determinism at resolution. E2-A, E2-A2 and E2-A3 tried to make extraction deterministic through regex over entity and property grammar. It reached 1.000 internally and fired on nothing external, because rules written for one corpus's grammar do not transfer. So the boundary was in the wrong place and the grammar-coverage audit is the evidence.

Two things to take. The resolution half is simple, auditable, model-free and better than what we have, which is nothing — our arms never had a merge step. And the resolve flag: extracted names are always resolvable because they are the extractor's guess, while a caller-supplied name can be taken literally, with the comment recording that a literal name must not become resolvable just because extraction agreed on the spelling. We lack that distinction and RARE-EXC is where it bites, since a flag must never be fuzzy-matched to its opposite and trigram similarity between them is high.

The assumption their mechanism rests on is also its limit, and it is a sharper research question than the one we were asking. Trigram similarity solves spelling variation and cannot solve referential variation: the new PM and Alice Chen share no trigrams. If their extractor does not already resolve that coreference, the merge step cannot. How often that matters is measurable and sits at the boundary of a mechanism that demonstrably works.

CANDIDATE-1 follows: a model extracts mentions into a controlled schema, deterministic trigram and union-find merge them with a literal escape hatch, and our addressing and temporal layers sit on top unchanged. The marginal contribution to measure is what our layers add on top of a resolution step that already works.
summary: Read from code. Entity mentions come from a structured LLM call; merging them is trigram similarity plus union-find with a deterministic canonical rule and no model at all.
title: Hindsight puts the model at extraction and keeps resolution deterministic; we put the boundary one step too early

body:
What the code shows is unchanged and remains verified at commit 3295716c. fact_extraction.py imports llm_interface and llm_wrapper and defines Pydantic response models; entity_processing.py names the result llm_entities. entity_resolver.py has no model in the merge path: pg_trgm trigram Jaccard verified byte-for-byte against Postgres, union-find with path halving, canonical name chosen most-mentioned then shortest then lexicographically smallest. The resolve flag distinguishing literal from resolvable names is real and is a distinction this project lacks.

The correction is one phrase. The superseded record said their mechanism demonstrably works. Reading code establishes how a thing is built and never that it beats an alternative, and no run on a shared harness has compared it to anything. Calling it demonstrated is the same claimed-versus-verified slip this project audits other people for, committed in its own sheet.

The accurate statement is that it is a well-motivated transplant candidate whose advantage is unmeasured.

A second correction follows and it is about order. Reading five repositories and then comparing them risks being persuaded by architecture rather than by results, and could mean reading fifty thousand lines to learn what a common harness would show in one run. The order inverts: every system on one arena with identical data, reader, prompt, budget, scoring and abstention policy, producing per-probe error vectors; then dissect only the modules that empirically won a category.

The Hindsight reading is not wasted, because it produced a design principle rather than a verdict: the boundary between language interpretation, which a model does well, and stable repeatable merging, which code does well. That principle is what CANDIDATE-1 is built on and it needed no benchmark to be worth having.
summary: The structural finding stands: extraction is a model call, resolution is deterministic trigram plus union-find. The superseded record called that mechanism demonstrably working, which no measurement here supports.
supersession_reason: reading code establishes construction, never comparative advantage; and the dissection order should follow the arena rather than precede it
title: Hindsight's boundary is verified from code; its resolver's advantage is unmeasured

body:
A first taxonomy had three classes and placed the OBSOLETE family under spelling variation. That was wrong. Five classes are needed: orthographic variation, lexical alias, referential variation, identity, and temporal state. OBSOLETE and the 48-near-clone failure are identity and temporal state, not spelling.

Trigram similarity answers whether two strings are the same name. Addressing answers whether two records are about the same object. Different axes.

The measurement makes the consequence concrete. service.billing/staging/endpoint.host against service.vault/staging/endpoint.host scores 0.707, while Alice Chen against Alice C. scores 0.583 and Microsoft Corp. against microsoft corporation scores 0.609. Any cutoff low enough to merge the spelling variants also merges two distinct services, and collision is a gate this project froze at below 0.02 before any of this was read. Lexical alias sits at 0.103 and referential at 0.000, below any usable cutoff, so trigram cannot reach them at all.

That does not make their mechanism wrong. It assumes it compares entity names, and in their pipeline those come from an extractor that names entities distinctly. Feeding it a composed address violates the assumption, because shared scope and property tokens dominate the trigram set while the distinguishing token is a small fraction of it.

So the transplant is conditional and the condition is precise: apply trigram resolution to the entity component alone, never to a composed address, and never to a value that must match exactly. The flag pair --dist=no against --dist=yes scores 0.417, which is why their resolve=false escape hatch is not optional in our setting.

One claim was also withdrawn. An earlier draft said classes two and three are untouched by anything either project built. Their extractor runs before the deterministic merge and may already resolve some aliasing and coreference — their own example of Alice, Alice Chen and the new PM reaching one person is a class three claim that nothing in entity_resolver.py could achieve. It is not known how much of classes two and three these systems resolve, or at which stage, and the shared arena is what would show it.
summary: Measured with Hindsight's own algorithm. Two distinct services score 0.707 similarity while two spellings of one person score 0.583, so class 4 overlaps class 1 and no single cutoff separates them.
title: No trigram threshold separates spelling variants from distinct services, and our corpus is the second case

body:
Hindsight compares entity names and is sound there. Applied to a composed address such as service.billing/staging/endpoint.host it is unsound, because the shared scope and property tokens dominate the trigram set while the only token that matters is a small fraction of it. The failure is caused by the representation rather than by the algorithm, which is why copying a mechanism without its representation level is a mistake rather than a shortcut.

Three rules follow, and each is entailed by the measurement instead of chosen.

Resolution is component-wise. Entity, property and scope resolve separately and the canonical address is composed from the resolved parts. Fuzzy-matching a composed string is the specific error measured above.

The data type determines the similarity policy, because the measurement refutes a global cutoff rather than merely discouraging one. A person name may be fuzzy. A service entity needs controlled alias resolution. A property identifier needs a canonical vocabulary. A flag, path, UUID or port is exact-only. A temporal value goes to the resolver.

Exactness belongs to the type, not to a caller's optional flag. The pair --dist=no and --dist=yes scores 0.417, high enough for an aggressive cutoff to merge them, and hoping a threshold stays conservative is not a policy.

The same measurement yields the arena's entity metrics, registered as a contract addendum rather than an edit: spelling merge recall, alias merge recall, coreference merge recall, identity collision rate and literal corruption rate. One accuracy figure hides the failure that matters, because a system can reach 0.95 on spelling variants and catastrophically merge distinct entities with both living inside the same number.
summary: Measured rather than asserted: trigram scores two distinct services at 0.707 and two spellings of one person at 0.583. Three design rules follow, each entailed by that measurement.
title: A similarity mechanism cannot be transplanted without the representation level it was designed for

body:
The plan after the Hindsight reading was a candidate combining their LLM extraction, their trigram resolver and our addressing and temporal layers. That is now held.

The reason is specific rather than cautious. The arena measures five entity classes separately: spelling, alias, coreference, identity collision and literal corruption. If it shows Hindsight weak on alias and coreference while another system is strong there, the transplant would have taken the wrong component, and no amount of code reading would have revealed it. Being persuaded by an architecture is the failure this order exists to prevent.

The generalisation is the larger finding and it goes beyond trigrams. A memory mechanism is not good or bad globally; it is correct for a particular representation and a particular failure mode. Trigram similarity is sound on entity names and unsound on composed addresses, measured at 0.707 against 0.583. Dense retrieval is sound on conceptual paraphrase and unsound on exact operational detail, measured on RARE-EXC at 1.000 lexical against 0.250 dense. A temporal resolver is decisive on future validity, overlap and conflict at 0.200 against 1.000, and a complete no-op on simple succession. Three mechanisms, three measurements, one shape.

So the arena's output should not be a leaderboard. Four systems within a few points of each other on an aggregate would say almost nothing, while a profile per failure mode with an error-correlation matrix and a cost column says what to compose. If each system turns out best on a different subset, the premise of a single optimal memory system fails, and the project's question changes from how to build the best memory to how to recognise which mechanism suits a given kind of information and query.

What blocks the arena is honest to state: adapters for five systems, infrastructure for those that need a database, and API budget for those whose extraction calls a model. That is the largest single piece of work this project has scheduled, and it is scheduled before any further code reading rather than after.
summary: The Hindsight transplant was planned and is now deferred. Reading code establishes how a mechanism works; it cannot establish that no other system does it better.
title: CANDIDATE-1 is not built until the arena says which system holds the best component for each failure mode

body:
The registered risk was that reset, ingest and query might unconsciously encode this project's own architecture, in which case a system failing to fit would be evidence against our interface rather than against that system. That is why the check came before the adapter.

CupMemEngine in pipeline.py exposes reset at line 58. write/writer.py defines write_session at line 244. query/engine.py defines answer_query at line 9. Their own run_sample calls reset once, then process_session per session, then the query engine per probe — the same three-phase shape, arrived at independently.

One difference is real and does not force a contract change. Their ingest is per session and carries a session_time, while the contract takes a list of records. An adapter groups records into a session and supplies the time, which is format translation rather than an exception, and is exactly the work an adapter is supposed to do.

The evidential value is that this is one independent architecture rather than a proof of generality. A second system fitting without exceptions would make the interface empirically supported rather than merely plausible; Hindsight and Graphiti are the next tests of it. Until then the honest statement is that the contract survived first contact with a system it was not designed around.

Cost of establishing this: reading three files. No adapter, no infrastructure, no spend, and the result would have been the same had it gone the other way — a contract that had to be changed for the first external system would have been a finding about our interface.
summary: CUPMem, written by another team for another benchmark, has reset, write_session and answer_query. That maps one-to-one onto the frozen contract's reset, ingest and query, and it was checked before writing any adapter.
title: The arena contract is not an AAMR abstraction: an independently built system exposes the same three methods

body:
The mapping is unchanged and verified: CupMemEngine.reset at pipeline.py line 58, write_session at write/writer.py line 244, answer_query at query/engine.py line 9, and their own run_sample calling reset once then process_session per session then the query engine per probe. A system built by another team for another benchmark exposes the same three-phase shape.

The correction is to what that licenses. The superseded record said the contract survived first contact. It establishes structural fit only.

Structural contract fit: the three method boundaries exist natively and nothing has to pretend to be an architecture it is not. PASS.

Operational contract fit: whether evidence identifiers, abstention, model calls, token counts, latency, reset semantics and query independence can be derived from that system honestly and without losing information. NOT TESTED. Only a written adapter run against the fixtures can answer it.

The distinction is worth carrying forward to Hindsight, Graphiti and Mem0, because a system can expose the right three methods and still be unable to report what it retrieved or what a query cost. If that happens the first question is not how to work around it but whether the arena should require that property at all, or whether it is required only because this project's own system happens to have it.

The evidential weight is also one architecture rather than a proof of generality. A second independent system fitting would make the interface empirically supported rather than plausible.
summary: CUPMem's reset, write_session and answer_query map onto the contract's three methods. That establishes the shape of the interface and says nothing yet about whether evidence, abstention, cost, tokens and latency can be derived from it without hacks.
supersession_reason: matching method names establishes the shape of an interface, not that its required outputs can be derived without hacks
title: Structural contract fit passes; operational contract fit is untested
